title: Launch: How AI Works
subtitle: Join the AI Creators Guild: what AI really is, how to talk to it, and how to stay safe while using it.
bigIdea: Generative AI doesn't 'know' things like a person — it predicts what probably comes next, based on patterns in huge amounts of training data. That's why clear prompts matter and why we always check its work.
objectives: Explain in their own words how a generative AI model makes text or images by predicting from patterns in training data.
Write a structured prompt using the Guild Prompt Recipe (Role · Task · Details · Style · Format) and improve it by iterating.
Identify an AI hallucination or bias and verify a claim with a trustworthy source.
Follow the AI Safety Pact: age rules, consent, privacy, honesty and copyright.
Describe how the course's XP, levels, houses and Boss Challenges work.

vocabulary.definition: Computer programs that do tasks that usually need human thinking, like recognising pictures or writing.
vocabulary.analogy: A very fast student who studied millions of examples but never went outside.
vocabulary.example: Your phone grouping photos by face.

vocabulary.definition: AI that creates new things — text, images, video, music, code.
vocabulary.analogy: A remix artist who learned from millions of songs and makes a new one.
vocabulary.example: Asking Gemini for a poem about pizza.

vocabulary.definition: The 'brain file' an AI uses, made by training on data.
vocabulary.analogy: A recipe book written by tasting a million meals.
vocabulary.example: GPT, Gemini and Claude are model families.

vocabulary.definition: The examples an AI learned from.
vocabulary.analogy: All the textbooks and practice tests a student studied.
vocabulary.example: Billions of web pages and captioned images.

vocabulary.definition: The instructions you give an AI.
vocabulary.analogy: Your order at a restaurant — the clearer it is, the better the meal.
vocabulary.example: 'Draw a cartoon cat astronaut, flat colors, square.'

vocabulary.definition: AI writes by guessing the most likely next piece of a word, again and again.
A small chunk of text (part of a word) the AI reads and writes.
When AI says something false but sounds confident.
vocabulary.analogy: A friend who'd rather make up an answer than say 'I don't know'.
vocabulary.example: Inventing a book that doesn't exist.

vocabulary.definition: When AI outputs are unfair or one-sided because of patterns in its training data.
vocabulary.analogy: If you only ever saw red apples, you'd think all apples are red.
vocabulary.example: Always drawing 'a scientist' as a man in a lab coat.

vocabulary.definition: Improving something step by step by trying, checking and changing.
vocabulary.example: Prompt v1 → v2 → v3, each better.

vocabulary.definition: The rules you agree to when you use an app, including minimum age.
vocabulary.analogy: The rules on the sign at the swimming pool.

vocabulary.definition: Fake but realistic media showing a real person doing or saying something they didn't.
vocabulary.analogy: A forged signature, but for faces and voices.
vocabulary.example: A fake video of a celebrity selling a scam product.

gamification.questLine: Join the Guild: create your nickname and avatar, learn the rules of AI, and earn your Safety Pact.
gamification.boss: Prompt Duel — houses battle to get the AI to produce a target output in the fewest prompt iterations, using the Prompt Recipe.
sideQuests: Teachable Machine Glitch Hunt: make your model confidently wrong and explain why (+25 XP).
Find a real news story about an AI hallucination and summarise it in 3 sentences with the source (+25 XP).
Write the Prompt Recipe as a rap/poem for the class wall (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Show the tools table; explain why ToS ages exist (COPPA protects under-13 data). No sneaking onto 13+/18+ apps — we use school accounts and teacher demos.
Webcam/photos of yourself only, and only in class tools. Never classmates. Discuss how a deepfake could hurt someone.
Guild nicknames; never type full name, school, address, phone or passwords into AI.
Hallucinations: AI predicts what SOUNDS right. Use the 'Two-Source Rule' for any fact.
Using AI is a skill, not cheating — when you say you used it. Introduce the #MadeWithAI label.

finalProject.title: Prompt Duel + AI Safety Pact
finalProject.brief: Each house receives target outputs (e.g. a 4-line poem with specific features, a recipe for 6 people with no nuts, an image of a specific scene). Using the Prompt Recipe, they iterate until they hit the target and document each version. Separately, each student writes and signs their own AI Safety Pact in their own words.
deliverables: Prompt log: v1, v2, v3… with what changed and why
Final output that matches the target
Personal AI Safety Pact (5 promises in your own words), signed by student (and optionally a parent)

levels: Recipe parts used precisely + constraints/examples added
3+ versions with a reason for each change
Changes are targeted and explained using vocabulary
Verified facts with a source and explained the error type
Promises include a 'what I'd do if…' scenario

finalProject.levelUp: Write a 'system prompt' that makes the AI act as a quiz-master for this module's vocabulary, then test it on a classmate and improve it twice.

support: Prompt Recipe card with sentence starters for each part.
Pair students: 'driver' types, 'navigator' reads the recipe aloud — swap every 10 minutes.
Vocabulary word wall with pictures (dual coding).
Exit tickets can be answered by drawing + labels.
extension: Compare the same prompt in two models and write 3 differences.
Explain temperature/randomness: run the same prompt 3 times and describe why answers differ.
Become a Guild Mentor for the build segment.

carryForward: The Prompt Recipe, the Safety Pact and the prompt log habit are used in every later module.
